samples.summary: The new `workflow_run.path` guard is applied to the three CI consumers but NOT to capture-collect.yml, which consumes `workflow_run` by DISPLAY NAME ("Agent Review Panel" / "Agent Review On-Demand") with no path, branch or head-repository clause — and it checks out another repository with `secrets.EVAL_STORE_TOKEN` and pushes to it.
samples.evidence: .github/workflows/capture-collect.yml:67-69 `workflow_run: workflows: ["Agent Review Panel", "Agent Review On-Demand"] types: [completed]`; the only job gate is line 129 `if: github.event_name != 'workflow_run' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion != 'skipped'` — no `path`, no `head_repository`, no branch restriction. Lines 142-146 then check out `dlgpdmsly2/wafflebase-agent-eval` with `token: ${{ secrets.EVAL_STORE_TOKEN }}` and the collector later pushes. The exact forgery the diff closes elsewhere (a second workflow file claiming a display name, pushable by anyone with workflows write on the base repo — the `agent:managed` human-PR threat model this change cites) reaches this consumer unchanged, and unlike docker-publish/publish-ghpage it is reachable from a PR branch because there is no `head_branch == 'main'` clause. docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1987-1990 enumerates the exempt consumers and never mentions capture-collect.yml, so it looks overlooked rather than deliberately excluded. Fix belongs on capture-collect.yml (add a `github.event.workflow_run.path` clause for the two producer files) or on the doc if the exposure is accepted.
searchedFor: read docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1981-1994 (the enumeration of which consumers need the clause)

samples.summary: docker-publish.yml and publish-ghpage.yml still identify CI by display name only; the new path guard was deliberately not extended to them, so a merged second file named `name: CI` drives a GHCR publish / gh-pages deploy of the tree it names.
samples.evidence: .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml:67-71 and .github/workflows/publish-ghpage.yml:41-47 gate on `conclusion == 'success' && event == 'push' && head_branch == 'main' && head_repository == github.repository` with no `path` clause, while both check out `github.event.workflow_run.head_sha` (docker-publish.yml:92, publish-ghpage.yml:55) and publish it. The diff's own comment in ci-report.yml (lines 49-52) and harness-engineering.md:1989-1990 argue the `main` clause means a forgery must be merged first, which is a real mitigation — but the residual is that after such a merge the deploy gate reads a run from an arbitrary file. Cheap to close by copying the one-line clause; flagged so the exemption is a decision rather than an omission.

samples.summary: New gate 1b makes every PR that touches `.github/workflows/**` or `.github/actions/**` un-promotable, and the panel's stalled/paging net does not cover that outcome — such a PR stays a draft with no failed job and no page, only a loop-status note.
samples.evidence: gate 1b returns false → `Not promoting: one or more gates are not satisfied` → exit 1 → the promote job's `1)` branch succeeds (agent-review-panel.yml:1539-1542). The stalled net keys on `needs.promote.result == 'failure'` (agent-review-panel.yml:2330), which a gates-unsatisfied exit 1 never produces, so nothing pages. Every subsequent CI round repeats the same non-promotion. This is documented as intended (harness-engineering.md:1905-1916, 'un-automated, a human flips it by hand'), but the human-notification path for it is only the sticky loop-status comment — worth confirming that is enough, since this branch itself (four workflow files) is in that class.
searchedFor: read agent-review-panel.yml promote job + stalled job gate at 2330

verdict.reason: The textual claim is accurate (capture-collect.yml:67-69 filters by display name only; :129 is the sole gate), but it is not a guard bypass. The identical job — same EVAL_STORE_TOKEN store checkout and push — is intentionally reachable with no workflow_run context at all via `schedule` (:74-75) and `workflow_dispatch` (:88-93), explicitly permitted by :129, so a `workflow_run.path` clause would close nothing the nightly sweep leaves open. The triggering run's identity is used only for a log line (:175-190, via env and quoted); nothing derives the checkout ref, run id or collection scope from the event, and a workflow_run run executes the default-branch file/checkout, so no forged-branch code executes in the token-holding job (the repo checkout also uses persist-credentials: false, :134-138). What can enter the store is bounded by artifact-prefix+window filtering (collect-captures.mjs:429-446), strict meta validation (:200-241) and write-once keys (:253-255) — all trigger-independent and equally reachable from the sweep, so the proposed fix is ineffective against the poisoning it posits. The clause's documented purpose (harness-engineering.md:1981-1990) is to protect arms holding contents: write that invoke the agent; this workflow is read-only (:101-103), and the posited forgery requires .github/workflows/** push access on the base repo, which already grants direct use of the secret. Residual impact is one redundant collection run — nit, not a major bypass.
